15.0.0.en: The tradition of the elders is the inherited teaching, handed down from fathers to sons among the Jews, for the interpretation of the Holy Scriptures and everything related to worship. It is a good and necessary thing, for from it the Apostle Paul knew the names of the two magicians who resisted Moses, Jannes and Jambres (2 Tim 3:8), and Jude knew the story of the dispute between the archangel Michael and Satan over the body of Moses the prophet (Jude 9).

15.0.1.en: So tradition is very important, and the Apostles in the New Testament commanded that it be held fast. But some of the elders of the Jews added strange teachings to the tradition, which God did not mention and which are against His commandments, among them the necessity of washing the hands before eating, and this is what the scribes rebuked the disciples of Christ for, because they did not carry out this tradition. For these scribes and Pharisees came from Jerusalem after the fame of Christ spread, not to learn anything from Him, but to oppose Him and to find fault with Him.

15.0.2.en: But the tradition of the elders that they mentioned is an additional thing of no value, because the washing of the hands mentioned in the Holy Scriptures was in other circumstances, for purification from certain sins (Lev 12-15).

15.1.0.en: Christ made clear to them that there are additions to the tradition of the elders that are not sound, and some of them are even against the commandments of God.

15.2.0.en: The commandment orders the honoring of father and mother (Ex 20:12), and likewise the Law punishes with death the one who despises or curses one of his parents (Ex 21:17). But a strange tradition was added by the elders of the Jews, that a person could offer a gift to the temple, and by this be exempted from honoring his parents, and this is against the spirit of the commandment, for how can the son neglect the needs of his parents on the basis of a sacrifice or offering he has made, and think that this pleases God?!

15.3.0.en: It is understood from the above that not every tradition among the Jews is sound, and this is what the Scripture calls the tradition of men, whereas sound tradition is very good.

15.3.1.en: Do not interpret the Holy Bible according to your personal opinion and your purposes, but hold fast to the teachings of the Church and the holy Fathers of the first generations, and submit to the interpretation of the universal Church, and you will understand the true meaning; and be occupied with applying the commandment more than with philosophical inquiries and debate to prove your opinions.

15.4.0.en: "Ye hypocrites": because you show something other than what is within you, which is that you hold to the law of God with exactness, while the truth is that you please your own purposes, namely offering money to the temple for your benefit, and neglecting the work of mercy even toward parents, and this is clearly against the commandments of God.

15.4.1.en: Isaiah showed this strange spirit of the scribes and Pharisees (Isa 29:13) (which is clinging to formal worship while the heart is far from God), and any addition to the word of God is the commandments of men, and is not from the commandments of God.

15.4.2.en: But if it is an oral word that God spoke to Moses and the prophets, or that Christ spoke to His disciples, then this is sound tradition.

15.5.0.en: "He called the multitude": His conversation with the scribes and Pharisees may have been on one side and not heard by the multitude that followed Him, or it may have been before the multitude, but He directed the speech to the people in order to teach them the spiritual truths, for He is bold, not fearing the opposition of the wicked, and always concerned for the truth.

15.5.1.en: "Hear, and understand": that is, listen with attention and awareness to what I say.

15.5.2.en: Christ wanted to bring the multitudes into the depths, so that they would not be content with the superficiality proclaimed by the Pharisees, which is the concern for washing the hands before eating, but would be concerned with what comes out from within a person and appears in his speech, for if it is evil, this defiles him.

15.5.3.en: And the words of Christ here have no connection with fasting, as the opponents of fasting claim, but are about washing the hands before eating. As for fasting, He affirmed it clearly many times, such as His teaching about fasting in His Sermon on the Mount (ch. 6:16-18).

15.6.0.en: "Then": after the multitudes and the scribes and Pharisees departed, Christ entered a house with His disciples (Mk 7:17), and this conversation took place.

15.6.1.en: "Were offended": they were angered and troubled, because He described them as hypocrites, since their teachings are the commandments of men and not the commandments of God, and He means the fifth of the Ten Commandments, concerning the honoring of parents. The disciples warned their Teacher that the Pharisees were troubled by His words, because He had exposed their hypocrisy and their clinging to teachings that are not from God, and which they attach to the tradition of the elders.

15.7.0.en: Christ made clear to them that submission to the word of God and freedom from hypocrisy are necessary, that we may be branches in the hand of God, who plants them in His Church, for however beautiful the plant may look, if God did not plant it, it will be rooted up and cast into the fire, because it is a tare and not wheat; so also are the hypocritical Pharisees.

15.8.0.en: He said to them: "Let them alone", meaning that they should disregard them and their teachings, perhaps that when the multitudes leave them they may repent.

15.8.1.en: And He declared that they are blind to the truth, worshiping their own honor and leading the Jews who follow them with teachings of error, and they are also blind by the misleading teachings of the Pharisees, and if the blind lead the blind, both fall into the pit of destruction... that is, He warns His disciples to keep away from the Pharisees and their misleading teachings, so that they would not be influenced by them and go astray from the truth.

15.8.2.en: Do not be troubled by the distress of the wicked at your words and conduct, but keep away from them so that you are not influenced by associating with them, and pray for them.

15.9.0.en: "Then answered Peter": Peter replied, and his question to Christ was not on his own behalf, but also on behalf of the rest of the disciples, for he said: "Declare unto us this parable", and afterward Christ addressed them all. "This parable": that is, the words of Christ mentioned in (v. 11), because he felt that it carried other meanings that needed clarification, so he called it a parable.

15.9.1.en: The disciples, and Peter the most impulsive of them, asked about the meaning of what Christ had said to the multitudes, and Christ marveled at their lack of understanding, after He had explained to them many earlier parables. But, with the gentleness of His fatherhood, He explained to them also His saying that the foods that enter the mouth are turned into nourishment that flows through the body, and the waste is disposed of, so it is material food that does not defile a person, but what harms him of it is disposed of, and these foods have no effect on the soul.

15.10.0.en: What comes out of a person's mouth, that is, from his heart, expresses him and he is held accountable for it, and not for what he eats.

15.10.1.en: Then He gave examples of sins, beginning with evil thoughts, as the source of actual sins, such as murder, adultery and theft.

15.10.2.en: And what is meant by fornication is a kind of adultery, and by blasphemies, abuse against God or people.

15.10.3.en: Be concerned for the purity of your speech and your conduct, and if you sin, repent, and hold yourself accountable for what is in your heart more than you are concerned with your outward appearance.

15.11.s.en: (3) The healing of the daughter of the Canaanite woman

15.11.0.en: Jesus departed from the region of Gennesaret, perhaps to keep away from the unprofitable discussions of the Pharisees, or from the crowding of the multitudes, and to show His love for the Gentiles, who are many in Tyre and Sidon, since He came for the salvation of the whole world.

15.11.1.en: "Tyre and Sidon": two cities on the Mediterranean Sea, west of Galilee, in present-day Lebanon.

15.12.0.en: "Have mercy on me": because her daughter's illness causes her great pain.

15.12.1.en: "Son of David": the Jews believed that the Messiah is the son of David, so when they saw the power of Christ and His miracles, they said that He is the son of David, that is, the Messiah. And when this Gentile woman heard of Christ, she called Him as the Jews title Him. When Christ passed by Tyre and Sidon, a Gentile woman came out to Him, of the descendants of Canaan the son of Ham the son of Noah. The Canaanites are the original inhabitants of the Promised Land, before the Jews came with Joshua. Her daughter was insane because a demon was in her (Mk 7:25), and she heard of the healing power of Christ, so she came out asking Him to heal her daughter.

15.13.0.en: Christ paid no attention, and went on His way. But she kept crying out, beseeching Him to heal her daughter, so that His disciples' hearts were moved with pity for her, and they asked Him to respond to her cry. And this is what Christ wanted, to move the hearts of the disciples and make them feel their responsibility for the salvation of the whole world, and not only the Jews.

15.14.0.en: Christ answered contrary to their request, declaring what the Jews thought and what He began with first, namely that He came for the salvation of the Jews who believe in God. But in truth He came to the Jews first, and then extended afterward to seek all the nations, as proved by His coming to these regions and performing the miracle.

15.14.1.en: And this method, that is, preaching to the Jews first, was fitting, because they thought that salvation was for them alone, and they would have rejected it if He had declared from the beginning of His preaching that His salvation was for the whole world. But after He convinced them that His salvation is spiritual and not material, from the Romans, He showed that it is a salvation for everyone in the whole world who believes in Him.

15.15.0.en: The woman believed that this was the awaited Messiah, the son of David, and that He is the Savior of the world. So she worshiped Him to declare her submission and her faith in Him, and asked Him to help her and heal her daughter.

15.16.0.en: Christ pretended not to accept her request, in order to reveal her faith and humility, so He told her that He had come for the salvation of the Jews, who are the children of God by their faith, and that it is not right for the grace of God that belongs to the children to be given and cast to the Gentiles, whom the Jews regard as dogs.

15.17.0.en: The woman's wonderful humility appeared, for she said to Him: the crumbs (the very small fragments) that fall from the children's table are enough for me. So she acknowledged that she was of the dogs, but that she needed His grace; and this also showed the extent of her faith and her persistence in prayer.

15.18.0.en: Finally, the purpose of Christ, His love and His concern for the Gentiles appeared in the person of this woman, for all that went before was to show the extent of her faith, her clinging to Him, her prayers and her humility. So He declared before the multitudes the greatness of her faith, and then granted the healing of her daughter, who returned well at once.

15.18.1.en: Hold fast to your prayers however long God's answer is delayed, so that you may acquire new virtues, such as humility, and then obtain what you desire; indeed, God will exalt you in His Kingdom before all the heavenly ones.

15.19.0.en: Christ returned from the borders of Tyre and Sidon beside the Mediterranean Sea to the Sea of Galilee, that is, the Sea of Tiberias, and went up into the mountain, which signifies being raised above earthly matters, so that those who go up to it declare their clinging to Him in their ascent, for they are not mere walkers on the road. He may have gone to the mountain seeking rest, but the multitudes came to Him and He attended to them.

15.20.0.en: "The God of Israel": it seems that the multitudes were Gentiles, and when Christ healed them they glorified the God of Israel, because they knew that Christ is a Jew.

15.20.1.en: The multitudes declared their need of Christ, so they brought to Him their beloved ones who were sick with various kinds of diseases, and He healed them all with His tenderness, so that the multitudes marveled at His divine authority in healing all kinds of diseases. And this signifies spiritually the power of Christ, to whom be glory, to heal everyone whose ability to speak, see or move has been hindered by sin, and all glorified God.

15.20.2.en: God is ready to heal all your diseases and to solve all your problems, especially the spiritual ones. But you must take refuge in Him with much prayer and humility, laying all your needs before Him, confident of His love, which is able to do everything for you.

15.21.s.en: (5) The feeding of the multitudes with the seven loaves

15.21.0.en: Christ continued His care for the multitudes, whether by healing their diseases, or by His spiritual teachings, or by answering their questions.

15.21.1.en: The time passed without their noticing, so that they spent three days with Him and did not ask for food, being occupied with His words and miracles. Perhaps they had eaten what they had brought from their homes on the first and second days, and on the third day they had no food left, for they did not expect to remain three days away from their homes, but the words of Christ drew them.

15.21.2.en: What matters is that Christ cared for their material needs, and spoke of it to His disciples to test their faith, especially after they had seen the feeding of the multitudes with the five loaves and the two fishes, but, sadly, they thought with their minds and not with their faith, and declared their inability to provide food for these multitudes in the wilderness, especially since most of the disciples were poor. Care for your spiritual life and rely on God, and be confident that what is difficult for you of your material needs He will provide for you.

15.22.0.en: Christ asked His disciples to look for the food that the multitudes had, and they found only seven loaves and a few little fishes.

15.22.1.en: The number seven signifies the Holy Spirit who works in the Holy Sacraments, which are able to satisfy all the spiritual needs of man.

15.23.0.en: Christ commanded His disciples to organize the multitudes, so they made them sit down so that it would be easy to distribute the food to them, and that they might behold quietly the greatness of the miracle. The wonder is that they believed they would eat, although they knew there was no food except the seven loaves and a few little fishes, but this is the faith that rises above reason and affects a person's conduct.

15.23.1.en: Christ took the bread and the fishes, and gave thanks, as in the previous miracle, to teach us to pray before taking food, and He blessed with His divine hand, and broke the bread and gave to His disciples to distribute from it, and likewise from the fish, to all the multitudes sitting on the ground; for the disciples are the priests of the New Testament responsible for distributing the gifts of God to all the faithful.

15.24.0.en: All ate, and their number was about four thousand men, besides women and children. And the number four signifies the four corners of the world, north and south, east and west, and the number thousand signifies heaven, that is, that the blessing of Christ is for the whole world, satisfying it and raising it to the heavenly life. After all had eaten, the disciples gathered the remaining fragments, and they filled seven baskets, and this also points to the work of the Holy Spirit, for He satisfies all and overflows.

15.24.1.en: And after Christ blessed the multitudes and sent them away, He boarded the ship on the Sea of Galilee and went to a city called Magdala.

15.24.2.en: The persecution of the Pharisees, bearing the cross

16.0.s.en: (1) The Pharisees ask for a sign

16.0.0.en: The Pharisees differ from the Sadducees, but their fear of Christ, to whom the multitudes were drawn and left them, made them agree to tempt Him, trying to show His weakness and to turn the multitudes away from Him. So they asked Him to perform for them a great miracle, appearing clearly in the sky or coming down from heaven, to confirm that He is the awaited Messiah, although He had performed many miracles before the multitudes. But in their pride and jealousy they did not believe in Him, and they still opposed Him. And they thought that by asking Him for a great sign from heaven they would reveal His inability to accomplish it, and the multitudes would turn away from Him.

16.1.1.en: "The sky is red": at sunset, when the disk of the sun begins to disappear, it gives a red color in the sky, and the clearer it is, the clearer the weather, because there are no clouds covering the red color.

16.1.2.en: "Red and lowering": the red color at sunrise, if it is not clear because clouds appear, means that the day is wintry and it may rain.

16.1.3.en: "The face of the sky": that is, the appearances of the weather from which you infer the weather conditions.

16.1.4.en: "The signs of the times": these are the prophecies that speak of Christ, then the appearance of John the Baptist who preceded Him, and also His many miracles that had not appeared before with such power in Israel, all of which confirm that He is the awaited Messiah. Christ did not give them a miracle, because He did not come to display His power before people, but to save them from sin. And He answered those who tempted Him that God had given them the mind with which they can discern the state of the weather, by the presence of a shining sun or of clouds. If they were able to discern the state of the weather, why did they not rather care to know the prophecies written about Him?! For this is their basic work as the religious leaders of the Jewish community, that they believe in Him and lead everyone to faith.

16.2.0.en: Christ made clear the reason for their lack of understanding, which is the evil of their hearts and their jealousy of Him. They clung to their selfishness and left God, so they became, spiritually, adulterers and fornicators, that is, they worshiped their pride instead of God. Therefore, He called them to repentance, saying to them that they did not need to see a sign from heaven, but should remember the story of Jonah the prophet and the people of Nineveh, and repent as they did, and then it would be easy for them to believe in Him. And He left them, grieved for them, so as not to waste His time in discussions without benefit.

16.2.1.en: Do not be much occupied with material requests from God, and know that your first need is repentance, that you may become pure, and be confident that if you care only for repentance, God will provide all your material needs.

16.3.0.en: The disciples crossed by ship from Magdala, on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, to the eastern shore. And in their absorption in service, they forgot their material needs, that is, taking food for the journey. The servant or the spiritual person forgets some of his material needs while occupied with God, but God provides for him.

16.4.0.en: Christ warned His disciples privately, away from the multitudes, of the leaven of the Pharisees, and by this He means their hypocrisy, for they teach exacting religious teachings, but in order to display their honor before people, and not out of love for God.

16.4.1.en: And leaven resembles hypocrisy, because it spreads inwardly in the dough without anyone sensing it, like the cunning of the hypocrite who pretends to be pious while his heart is far from the love of God.

16.4.2.en: But the disciples thought He was speaking of the leaven of material bread, that is, He was reminding them that they had forgotten to take food for the journey.

16.5.0.en: The words of Christ exposed a sin in the hearts of the disciples, namely their preoccupation with material needs, for they were troubled because they had forgotten the food needed for the journey. So Christ rebuked them, reminding them of His miracles of feeding the multitudes with the five loaves or the seven loaves, and how they were filled and twelve baskets or seven baskets were left over. They should have relied on Him, confident of His ability to provide for their material needs, and focused only on the service.

16.6.0.en: Then the disciples understood the purpose of Christ, that He was warning them of the teachings of the Pharisees, full of hypocrisy, that is, He was calling them to simplicity of heart and the love of God and of everyone.

16.6.1.en: Do not rejoice in your ability to pretend to what is not within you in order to reach your purposes, for this makes you divided against yourself, and people with time do not trust you; but apply in your life what you believe, and if there is evil within you, repent of it and be rid of hypocrisy.

16.7.0.en: Christ wanted to direct His disciples to knowing Him and believing in His divinity, so He asked them what is the people's belief concerning Him?

16.7.1.en: The disciples replied that there are many opinions, for some, like Herod, think that He is John the Baptist risen from the dead, and some say that He is Elijah who ascended to heaven in his body and has returned to earth, for the Jews were awaiting the coming of Elijah before the coming of the Messiah, based on the prophecy of Malachi (Mal 4:5-6), (and others think He is Jeremiah the prophet, and some said that He is one of the ancient prophets who has risen, because of the similarity of His message with the message of the prophets who called people to repentance in preparation for eternity, but they could not understand anything about His divinity.

16.8.0.en: Then Christ moved to the important question, which is the faith of His disciples concerning Him, and Peter answered on behalf of the disciples, declaring that they believe in Him as the awaited Messiah, the Son of God, that is, God incarnate.

16.9.0.en: "Flesh and blood": that is, a human being.

16.9.1.en: "My Father which is in heaven": by the Spirit of God, for it is a revelation from heaven by the power of God, because faith in the incarnate Christ rises above reason and human logic.

16.9.2.en: Christ praised the faith of Peter which he declared, and it is clear that this was by the grace of God and not from human logic, because the mystery of the Incarnation surpasses reason; for how does God condescend, in His love and humility, to unite with our humanity?!

16.10.0.en: Christ affirmed the importance of this declared faith, for upon the rock of faith the Church is built, so the basis of anyone's membership in the Church is his faith that Christ is God. And He declared that Satan and hell have no authority over the Church, for her children, the faithful, after this life are transferred to the paradise of bliss and the Kingdom of Heaven.

16.10.1.en: And He did not say to him, You are the rock, but said: "Thou art Peter", to make clear that the rock is the rock of faith upon which the Church is built, and not Peter.

16.11.0.en: "Keys": He likened the Church to a locked treasure, and gave the keys to the Apostles and their successors, the bishops and priests, to give from God absolution through forgiveness to the one who repents, or binding and withholding from the Holy Sacraments from the one who refuses repentance.

16.11.1.en: "The kingdom of heaven": that is, the Church, where God reigns over the hearts of His faithful children, and this Church extends forever.

16.11.2.en: Since Christ had spoken of the Church in which the Holy Spirit works, He declared the sacrament of confession, in which authority is given to the Apostles, which is the authority of loosing and binding. So everyone who persists in his sins, they bind his sins upon him, and he is not worthy to partake of the Holy Sacraments, and everyone who repents and confesses them, they loose him from them and give him the Sacraments.

16.11.3.en: Christ gave this authority to Peter as the representative of the priesthood of the New Testament, that is, to all the disciples and their successors, the bishops and priests, and He will repeat the same authority once more in (ch. 18:18).

16.11.4.en: And this is the first clear declaration of the institution of the sacrament of repentance and confession, one of the seven sacraments of the Church, and He declared it early because of its importance, since repentance is the entrance to the whole spiritual life.

16.12.0.en: After His clear declaration of His divinity, He charged His disciples not to speak of this matter to the multitudes, lest they stir up the envy of the Pharisees and the religious leaders, and hinder the people's faith in Him. And after the accomplishment of redemption on the cross and the announcement of His resurrection, this teaching will strengthen their faith.

16.12.1.en: Your faith in Christ makes you not troubled by the changes of the world, but rejoicing in fellowship with Him, and preparing for being with Him always in His heavenly Kingdom, and it also drives you to serve Him in drawing distant souls so that they enter His Kingdom.

16.13.s.en: (4) The necessity of bearing the cross

16.13.0.en: "The elders": the leaders of the Jews, members of their highest council, which is the Sanhedrin (ch. 5:21-22).

16.13.1.en: "The chief priests": the current high priest, the former chiefs, and the heads of the divisions of the priests.

16.13.2.en: "The scribes": the copyists and teachers of the Law.

16.13.3.en: After Christ declared His divinity to His disciples, and the founding of His Church which stands forever, it was necessary to declare the price of establishing this Church, that is, the shedding of His blood on the cross. So He made clear to His disciples the necessity of the sufferings He would receive from the elders and chief priests, which would lead in the end to His death to redeem mankind; but He would rise afterward on the third day. For after they knew His divinity, they could understand His resurrection, and not be troubled by His sufferings.

16.14.0.en: "Took him": Peter thought that the words of Christ about His sufferings were a kind of emotion resulting from the great opposition of the Jews to Him, so he tried to prevent Christ from speaking these words, lest it affect the rest of the disciples with grief and despair.

16.14.1.en: "Rebuke": he tries to prevent Him from continuing these talks.

16.14.2.en: "Be it far from thee": Peter believed in His divinity, and he and the rest of the disciples did not understand the idea of redemption, and he saw that sufferings contradict His power.

16.14.3.en: "Satan": because his thinking is satanic, as he thinks of the earthly kingdom and not the heavenly kingship. "An offence": you are trying, Peter, to hinder the redemption of mankind.

16.14.4.en: "Those that be of men": that is, the earthly kingship, and not the thought of God, which is the redemption of mankind.

16.14.5.en: The disciples were affected by what Christ would suffer, because He demolished the idea of the earthly kingdom, which they believed in with the rest of the Jews, and Peter rushed to prevent Christ from handing Himself over to the priests by going to Jerusalem. But Christ rebuked Peter because he was hindering the redemption of mankind, by his clinging to the earthly kingship and his position in this kingdom, forgetting the most important thing, which is the Kingdom of Heaven.

16.15.0.en: Christ declared the two conditions of following Him in order for a person to become a member of this Church, which are: (1) denying oneself, that is, humility.

16.15.1.en: (2) bearing the cross, that is, enduring sufferings for the sake of holding to the faith and the commandments of God.

16.15.2.en: And since the way seemed hard, Christ made clear that saving the soul from the sins of the world requires losing it, in the sense of rejecting and putting to death every evil desire in the soul, and whoever loses his soul, that is, bears the cross for the sake of Christ, rescues it from being lost in the evils of the world, and finds a place for it in the Kingdom.

16.16.0.en: On the other hand, if a person permits himself the lusts of the world, and even if we imagine that he possessed every desire in him, he will lose his eternity, and by this he will have lost everything, because there is nothing equal to this soul or compensating for it. For a person has one soul and cannot find another, and it is more precious than all the possessions of the world and its lusts, and its price is the blood of Christ shed for it, so a person cannot lose the most precious thing in existence, which is himself, for the sake of any temporary material desires.

16.17.0.en: "The Son of man": Christ is not ashamed to call His name in heaven the Son of Man, for as He shared with us weakness in the body on earth, He makes us share with Him in the heavenly glory, and remains among us as the firstborn among many brethren.

16.17.1.en: Here Christ warns them of the Day of Judgment, when He comes in the glory of His Father with His angels, and judges every person according to his faith, his love for Him, and all his works.

16.17.2.en: By this He reassures His followers that what they endure on earth, they will receive its reward on the Day of Judgment. And on the contrary, the wicked who delighted in sin will be punished on that day.

16.18.0.en: The coming of the Son of Man in His kingdom may be meant to refer to His transfiguration on the mountain before His three disciples: Peter, James and John.

16.18.1.en: It may also be that what is meant is the spread of faith in Christ and His reign over hearts in the different countries of the world, and this was witnessed by many of the disciples who lived a long time, such as John the Beloved who lived until near the end of the first century.

16.18.2.en: Do not be dazzled by the passing lusts of the world, or occupied with its cares and the needs of the body. And do not let your standards be material like the rest of people, but seek the salvation of your soul through the growth of your relationship with God and the service of others, preferring the work of mercy to your own comfort, and accept with joy all the sufferings that God permits for you, training yourself each day to control your desires and to use everything in measure, so that your feelings may be released in love toward God, and you prepare yourself for eternity.
